column1: # aes-m05-addrin.tsv -- the proof that a case can hand an AES call a POINTER.
# Read by DUMPAES (core/dumpaes.c), area 5, record 120 bytes.  Loader, column
# format and the guard: core/cases.h.  Eight columns, not seven: this is the
# first table that declares "!columns 8" and therefore the first that carries
# an addr_in column.  Everything written before it stays seven columns and
# means exactly what it always meant -- that is the point of the directive.
# WHAT THE COLUMN IS FOR
# Roughly a dozen AES opcodes do all of their work behind a pointer, and a
# case table could not state one: it is ONE FILE carried to two machines, and
# an address is different on each.  So the table names a BUFFER BY NUMBER and
# the dumper fills in its own address, the way cases/vdi-raster.tsv names its
# two pixel buffers.  Each buffer is TD_AES_BUF_BYTES long and is laid before
# every call with eight printable characters, a NUL and a canary
# (core/tosdump.h, core/record.c td_aes_buf_fill), identically on both
# targets -- a buffer that differed would make the case measure the buffer
# instead of the function.  Buffer 0 reads "ABCDEFGH", buffer 1 "HIJKLMNO".
# This table is deliberately SMALL.  It exists to show that the mechanism
# carries on both machines, not to cover the opcodes it unlocks; the table
# that does that is a separate piece of work.
# WHAT IT ASKS, case by case
#   A  An ordinary case in the new form, planting nothing ("-").  It is here
#      so that the eight column form is shown to express the seven column
#      form's meaning unchanged.
#   B  appl_find (13), the smallest call that is nothing but a pointer read:
#      AP_PNAME is addr_in[0] (aesdefs.h:165, gemsuper.c:107) and ap_find
#      does one strncmp per process against it (gemaplib.c:95-108,
#      gempd.c:38-57).  Neither buffer's first eight characters are the name
#      of any AES process, so BOTH machines must answer -1 -- which is what
#      makes this the case that proves the pointer arrived: with a poisoned
#      one the TT would not have got this far.
#   C  wind_get WF_NAME (104/2) on a window that really HAS a title.  This is
#      the case the whole exercise was for.  EmuTOS' wm_get has no arm for
#      WF_NAME at all and falls into "default: return FALSE"
#      (gemwmlib.c:1591-1592); NewTOS answers it and copies the title out
#      (tos-api/src/aes/window.rs, the WF_NAME | WF_INFO arm).  So RET_CODE
#      is expected to be 0 on the TT and 1 on NewTOS -- TASK/A42.md, measured
#      here for the first time.
#   D  The same call on a window with NO title.  NewTOS returns FALSE for an
#      empty title too, so C and D together separate "answers the field" from
#      "answers because the window happens to have a name".
# THE TITLE IS SET THROUGH THE int_in WORDS, NOT THROUGH addr_in, and that is
# not a choice: EmuTOS' wm_set reads the string pointer as *(char **)pinwds
# with pinwds = &int_in[2] (gemwmlib.c:1661 via gemsuper.c:346) and looks
# nowhere else.  The dumper packs it there at the TARGET's own pointer width
# -- four bytes on the m68k, eight on AArch64 -- which is what the classic
# GEM binding does (gemlib a_wind_set_str.c:25) and what both AESs read back
# (NewTOS: tos-api/src/aes/mod.rs, intin_ptr).  IN_LEN 6 covers the wider of
# the two, so one line is correct on both.  Such a plant is allowed only on a
# PRELUDE, because a packed pointer occupies two WORDs on one machine and
# four on the other and int_in is recorded -- see core/cases.h.
# WHAT THE RECORD SHOWS AND WHAT IT DOES NOT.  A planted addr_in slot records
# the buffer's TOKEN (0xB0FF0000 + n), not its address: the address differs
# between the two machines by construction and would fabricate a difference
# in every case.  The 120 byte AES record has no room for the BUFFER'S
# CONTENTS, so what NewTOS copied into buffer 0 in case C is not in the dump;
# RET_CODE is.  A record that carried the buffer would be a different record
# size and would invalidate every dump already taken.
# OUT_LEN IS 1 WHEREVER ONLY THE RETURN CODE IS ASKED FOR.  xif copies
# exactly OUT_LEN words back out of an UNINITIALISED stack buffer
# (gemsuper.c:429-432, :444-445), so a wind_get that returns FALSE with
# OUT_LEN 5 would deliver four words of the TT's stack -- a difference that
# measures the stack and not the AES.  With OUT_LEN 1 the surplus slots stay
# poisoned on both.
# A case id is the PHYSICAL LINE NUMBER and this file's CRC binds every dump
# to it, so ANY edit -- an appended case, a fixed typo in a comment --
# invalidates every dump already taken with it.  This file is written ONCE.
# The reset is the AES' own: wind_new closes and deletes every window with a
# handle >= 1 and drains the wind_update locks (gemwmlib.c:1875-1893), which
# is what lets section C create and open handle 1 twice without the second
# half inheriting the first.
!reset
!columns
# A -- the eight column form, planting nothing

column8: graf_handle, an ordinary case in the new form

column1: # B -- appl_find, a pure pointer read

column8: appl_find "ABCDEFGH": no process has that name

column1: # C -- wind_get(WF_NAME) on a window that has a title (A42)

column8: open it, so the title is live
wind_set WF_NAME = buffer 1, packed at int_in[2]

column1: # D -- the same call, no title set

column8: wind_get WF_NAME with no title set
